title: Exit tickets that shape tomorrow
hook: An exit ticket takes three minutes at the end of a lesson and can save you a whole lesson of reteaching.
coreIdeaMd:
An **exit ticket** is one or two questions answered on a slip of paper before students leave.

- Ask about the **main idea** of the lesson, not the hardest question.
- Sort them into three piles straight after: **got it**, **nearly**, **not yet**.
- Start the next lesson with what the piles tell you, for example a two-minute reteach for the "not yet" pile while others start the warm-up.

Exit tickets don't need marks or comments. Their job is to change what you do tomorrow.

checkItems.stemMd: What is the main purpose of an exit ticket?
options: To give each student a mark
To decide what to do at the start of the next lesson
To keep students busy at the end of class
checkItems.answer: To decide what to do at the start of the next lesson
checkItems.feedbackCorrect: Yes. It is information for you, not a test for them.
checkItems.feedbackIncorrect: An exit ticket is information for your planning. Sorting into three piles is quicker than marking.

tryTomorrow: Finish tomorrow's lesson with a one-question exit ticket. Sort them into three piles before you leave school.
reflectPrompt: How would sorting into three piles change the way you start your next lesson?
